input: Registered checked Operation action bindings, exact fields, complete selected factory bindings and the same checked graph and composition boundary.
definition: A Rust Operation is an async native action over borrowed domain inputs, owned Event inputs and an explicit transaction store. It coordinates declared reads, Rules, factory validation, Event construction and one atomic state-and-outbox commit.
transaction: A generated Store trait begins one generated Transaction. Read methods are typed by slot and identity. Precommit failures await rollback. Commit receives one operation-specific typed batch and returns committed, rejected or indeterminate. Commit error is uncertain; no rollback or retry follows a commit attempt.
values: Read identities, guard arguments, writes and results are statically lowered from checked value expressions. Returned and committed values cross explicit owned boundaries. Selected generated factories validate Entity and Value Object writes/results; invariant references never invent validators.
events: Each declared Event input is consumed exactly once after guards and value validation. Generated-time Events receive an explicit borrowed slot clock. Event construction is data-only; commit is the only publication-capable boundary.
module: One collision-free module per qualified selector under src/application/operations plus exact Rule, factory and Event dependency artifacts.
verification: Deterministic planning, real Cargo async execution, commit disposition and uncertainty observations, exactly-one commit evidence, no post-attempt rollback, and transaction/provider compile-fail controls are required.
claim_ceiling: Generated orchestration under an explicit provider contract; not provider isolation, durability, exactly-once delivery or automatic recovery.
compatibility: Legacy typed Operation v1 and existing generators remain unchanged. This candidate requires explicit checked action bindings and has no default cutover.
